title: Pronoun Order - Two Pronouns before the Verb
description: Put two object pronouns in order before the verb: {je te le donne}, {je le lui donne}.
can_do: Put two pronouns before the verb in order: {je te le donne}.
Replace both objects of a sentence: {je donne le livre à Marie} becomes {je le lui donne}.
line: Object pronouns go before the verb, and two pronouns always come in the same order: {te le}, {le lui}.

parts.heading: One pronoun, before the verb
text: An object pronoun goes in front of the verb it belongs to.

pairs: Will you give me your number?

parts.heading: {me}, {te}, {nous} and {vous} come first
text: When a sentence has {me}, {te}, {nous} or {vous} and also {le}, {la} or {les}, the first group goes first.

build.k: le livre becomes le: te + le

build.fr: Je donne le livre à Marie.
build.en: I give the book to Marie.

parts.heading: With {ne … pas}
text: {ne} goes in front of both pronouns, and {pas} goes after the verb. The pronouns stay together.
parts.note: In a positive command, the pronouns move after the verb: {donne-le-moi}.

pairs: Je ne te le donne pas.
I'm not giving it to you.
Je ne le lui donne pas.
I'm not giving it to him.

checks.ask: Which one means “I give it to you”?
Which one means “I give it to him”?
checks.why: {le} is the thing and {lui} is the person, and {le} comes first: {je le lui donne}.

checks.ask: Which one means “I'm not giving it to her”?

options.text: Je ne le lui donne pas.
Elle ne me le donne pas.

checks.why: {ne} goes before both pronouns and {pas} after the verb: {je ne le lui donne pas}.
